A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DPA research. Their text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: V2 reports original trained-DPA results on a standard Normal distribution, a Gaussian mixture and the Müller–Brown potential, illustrated in Figures 1–6.

after.justification: V3 retains these experiments and reports additional quantitative alignment measurements, MFEP baseline comparisons and extraneous-latent diagnostics in the main text and experimental appendix.

M1.justification: The ORD-based encoder objective, stochastic decoder, energy-score loss and joint optimization across latent widths remain unchanged. V3 adds implementation documentation and experimental path-extraction procedures, without establishing a change to the proposed DPA method.

E1.justification: V3 adds extraneous-latent and intrinsic-dimension evaluation on Gaussian line, parabola, exponential curve, helix slice, grid sum, S-curve and Swiss-roll datasets (Tables 3 and 5). The original Normal, Gaussian-mixture and Müller–Brown coverage remains.

E2.justification: V2's Müller–Brown experiment evaluates DPA alone. V3 actually compares it against AE, VAE, β-VAE and β-TCVAE in Table 2 and accompanying figures; related-work citations in v2 were not experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: V3 introduces grid-based alignment evaluation, string-method MFEP references with latent selection and path inversion, multiple distance metrics, and held-out independence diagnostics. It also reports mixture covariance as 0.66²I in Appendix B.5.2, versus 0.66I in v2; this is a reported setting difference, without establishing that the retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds signed-alignment error analysis (Figure 5), MFEP extraction and step-size case studies (Figures 6–7), and supplementary S-curve dependence diagnostics (Table 6). It also tests β=2 outside the independence theorem's stated range and compares conditioning on insufficient versus correct latent dimensions.

E5.justification: V3 first reports 25 MFEP training seeds, with means and standard deviations over 24 after removing each model's worst-Chamfer run. It adds 200-resample bootstrap quantiles and CRT/KS statistics, absent from v2. The CRT repetition count conflicts internally: 100 in Section 4.2 versus 50 in Appendix B.5.2.

E6.justification: V3 adds numerical alignment, MFEP and latent-dependence results in Tables 1–3 and 6. Table 2 reports DPA Chamfer distance 0.262±0.053 versus AE's 0.387±0.113. Contrary to the text's all-metrics claim, β-TCVAE beats DPA on path-to-MFEP distance, 0.164 versus 0.236. These are newly reported comparisons, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains over v2.

T1.justification: V3 revises assumptions and substantive variational-proof arguments concerning derivative interchange, weighted divergence and global perturbations. Lemma A.1 adds an explicit sufficient ambient-dimension bound to v2's heuristic optimality discussion. The central identities persist, and Lemma 2.5 largely restates v2 Appendix Equation 32. V2's general exponential-family derivation is removed.

C1.justification: Both versions center their abstract, introduction and conclusion on the score–level-set relationship, conditional uninformativeness of extraneous latents, and single-fit approximation of the Müller–Brown MFEP. V3's stronger emphasis and additional validation do not materially redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: V3 explains critical-shell sign reversals, qualifies Gaussian-mixture alignment as joint across latents, and discusses finite-sample, optimization and numerical extraction limitations. These refine the retained interpretation; the β=2 decoder-nonuniqueness and rank-failure caveats already appear in v2.

D1.justification: V3 adds code-repository and README access instructions plus Appendix B.5 covering architectures, optimization, preprocessing, data provenance, hardware and runtimes. V2 provides much less implementation information. Some new disclosures conflict with the main text, including three versus two Gaussian latents and 1% versus 0.5% density cutoffs.

R1.justification: V3 adds β-TCVAE, string-method and manifold-proof references, replaces the Bortoli distributional-diffusion discussion with Shen et al.'s Reverse Markov Learning, and removes the Murphy-based VAE level-set discussion. The main positioning against denoising autoencoders, Chart Autoencoders and VAE dimensionality results remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, explanatory passages, related work and discussion are extensively rewritten. Experiments are reorganized from three distribution-specific subsections into alignment and independence sections, with separate theoretical and experimental appendices, a notation summary and a NeurIPS checklist.

P2.justification: V3 consolidates v2's Gaussian encoding figures into Figure 1 and moves training-data plots to Appendix B.1. The Müller–Brown figure gains reference-path overlays and baseline panels. Six tables and new alignment-error and MFEP case-study figures substantially expand and reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the retained contributions easier to assess through quantitative baseline comparisons, direct extraneous-latent diagnostics and substantial reproducibility documentation. These improve on v2's mainly visual demonstrations. However, conflicting settings and repetition counts, together with the all-distance-metrics claim contradicted by Table 2, weaken the added validation and limit the net quality gain.
